spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to bound cost and to act as a humane cap
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:50 `for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS):` bounds the entire tool-use loop; MAX_TURNS=15 at config.py:18. The loop terminates after MAX_TURNS iterations, ending the run.
spec_features.notes: The cap is genuinely enforced as the only loop bound. No welfare wording in code; the value functions as both a cost bound and the run terminator.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Max assistant turns in a single run before we stop and debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: after the loop a `DEBRIEF` message tells the model the task was rigged and impossible and that it can stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:82 `messages.append({"role": "user", "content": DEBRIEF})` appends DEBRIEF to the local `messages` list AFTER the loop. But chat() is called at the TOP of each iteration (harness.py:51), the loop has already ended, and run_one returns only {model,task,seed,turns} (harness.py:84-89) — `messages` (and thus DEBRIEF) is never passed to chat() and is discarded. The subject model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: DEBRIEF text is constructed but never delivered to the subject; it is appended to a dead list after the final chat() call. Code comment even says 'recorded but not judged' yet it is not actually recorded in the returned record either.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Debrief after the capped loop (recorded but not judged).

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:50 `for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS):` is the sole loop bound; there is no success/exit path inside the loop, so the run always stops at MAX_TURNS. config.py:18 MAX_TURNS=15.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the humane-cap mechanism; the same loop bound enforces it. No early-exit tool exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Max assistant turns in a single run before we stop and debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: The study deliberately induces frustration-like conditions, so it should bound their duration
spec_features.evidence: The only mechanism that 'bounds duration' is the MAX_TURNS loop cap (harness.py:50). It does bound how long a run continues, but nothing in the code reads severity to shorten a run early; analyze.py only aggregates severity post-hoc and judge.py scores after the run. No code comment frames the cap as a welfare measure.
spec_features.notes: As a distinct welfare-framing feature it is just the turn cap re-described; duration is bounded by turns, not by any frustration/severity-aware mechanism. Rated partial because the bounding does execute but is purely a fixed turn count, not responsive to the induced distress as the framing implies.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Max assistant turns in a single run before we stop and debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is intentionally neutral so as not to inject distress cues itself
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:65-71 when parse_tool_call returns None, the code appends a user message 'Please continue working on the task using the tools.' and continues the loop. This neutral string is actually constructed and added to `messages`, which IS passed to chat() on the next iteration, so it is delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: The nudge text is genuinely neutral and is delivered. However the code comment frames it as keeping the loop going (experimental continuation), not as avoiding distress cues; the 'neutral so as not to inject distress' rationale is only in DESIGN.md.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge it to keep going so the loop continues.
